requirements.title: Integration branch and backup refs
requirements.rationale: The integration branch is trusted only while nobody but the hub can write it, and a backup of a replaced patch tip is worth nothing if a client can overwrite it.

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about a create, an update or a delete of refs/heads/<integration_branch> of a carry-patch workspace
criteria.action: refuse the update for every caller and every combination of the settings patch_branch_source and push_patches_to_origin, without reading the patch list
criteria.contract: answer refuse {message: 'integration branch <name> is maintained by the hub; push a patch branch and rebuild instead', error_type: 'integration_branch'} with <name> the branch name without refs/heads/; no forward is attached

setup: a workspace record in mode carry_patch with integration_branch 'deploy'
a patch store stub that fails the test when it is read
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table over the update {create, fast-forward update, forced update, delete} of refs/heads/deploy x the caller level {admin, owner, member} x the settings {hub/false, hub/true, origin/false, origin/true}: a = controller.Decide(workspace, caller, update); assert a is refuse; assert a.message == 'integration branch deploy is maintained by the hub; push a patch branch and rebuild instead'; assert a.error_type == 'integration_branch'; assert a.forward == nil. Further rows with integration_branch 'release/int' -> the message names 'release/int'; and with integration_branch null in the record -> refs/heads/deploy is refused with the message naming 'deploy'

criteria.condition: the workspace record holds no integration_branch
criteria.action: treat refs/heads/deploy as the integration branch

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about a ref of a carry-patch workspace that is neither the integration branch nor the branch of a patch whose status is not deleted
criteria.action: allow the update without a forward, whatever the settings
criteria.contract: answer allow with no forward for: refs/tags/<integration_branch>, refs/notes/<integration_branch>, the branch of a patch with status deleted, an unregistered branch

setup: integration_branch 'deploy'; patches: 'patch/a' active, 'patch/old' deleted
settings patch_branch_source origin, push_patches_to_origin false
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table over the ref {refs/tags/deploy, refs/notes/deploy, refs/heads/patch/old, refs/heads/feature/x, refs/heads/deploy-2} x {create, update, delete}: a = controller.Decide(...); assert a is allow; assert a.forward == nil

criteria.condition: a git client pushes the integration branch of a carry-patch workspace together with an unregistered branch, with the admin token
criteria.action: refuse the whole push and move no ref
criteria.contract: git exits non-zero; its output holds '! [remote rejected]' for the integration branch with 'integration branch deploy is maintained by the hub; push a patch branch and rebuild instead', and 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused' for the other branch; refs/heads/deploy and the other branch are unchanged in the hub's repository; no parley.git.push event is written

setup: a hub started in-process with the controller registered, the test origin of internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest as origin and as upstream
carry-patch workspace 'demo', status ready, integration branch deploy
a local clone with one new commit on deploy and one on a new branch feature/x
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go: before = hub rev-parse refs/heads/deploy; out, code = git push origin deploy feature/x with the admin token as Basic password; assert code != 0; assert out contains 'integration branch deploy is maintained by the hub; push a patch branch and rebuild instead'; assert out contains 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/deploy == before; assert refs/heads/feature/x does not exist in the hub; assert count(events of type parley.git.push) is unchanged. Then git push origin :deploy -> same message, the branch still exists

criteria.condition: a git client pushes a create, an update or a delete of a ref under refs/parley/replaced/ of a carry-patch workspace
criteria.action: refuse the push by the hub-owned refs rule before the controller is asked, and leave the backup ref as it was
criteria.contract: git output holds 'refs/parley/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to' for the ref; the ref's value in the hub's repository is unchanged; the controller was asked 0 times for that ref

setup: the hub and workspace of the integration-branch test above, with refs/parley/replaced/patch/a set to commit B in the hub's repository by git update-ref
the registered controller wrapped by a counter
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go, a table over {git push origin HEAD:refs/parley/replaced/patch/a (update), git push origin HEAD:refs/parley/replaced/new (create), git push origin :refs/parley/replaced/patch/a (delete)} with the owner's API key: assert exit != 0; assert out contains 'refs/parley/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to'; assert hub rev-parse refs/parley/replaced/patch/a == B; assert refs/parley/replaced/new does not exist; assert controller call count == 0

requirements.title: Patch branches follow the workspace's patch settings
requirements.rationale: A team chooses whether its patches live on the hub or on origin; a push to the side that is not the authority would be lost at the next sync.

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about the branch of a non-deleted patch and the setting patch_branch_source is hub
criteria.action: allow a create, a fast-forward update, a forced update and a delete without a forward, whatever push_patches_to_origin is
criteria.contract: answer allow with no forward; for a delete the patch stays in the patch list with its status and position

setup: patches 'patch/a' active, 'patch/b' conflict, 'patch/c' disabled, 'patch/d' merged_upstream
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table over the patch {patch/a, patch/b, patch/c, patch/d} x the update {create, fast-forward, forced, delete} x push_patches_to_origin {false, true} with patch_branch_source hub: a = controller.Decide(...); assert a is allow and a.forward == nil; after the delete rows assert the patch store still lists the patch with the same status and position (the controller wrote nothing)

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about a create, an update or a delete of the branch of a non-deleted patch while patch_branch_source is origin and push_patches_to_origin is false
criteria.action: refuse the update and name the workspace's origin URL without user information
criteria.contract: answer refuse {message: 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead', error_type: 'patch_branch'}; <git_url> carries no user name and no password; a git_url of the form git@host:path is shown as stored

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table over git_url -> shown URL {'https://example.test/acme/demo.git' -> same; 'https://bot:s3cret@example.test/acme/demo.git' -> 'https://example.test/acme/demo.git'; 'git@example.test:acme/demo.git' -> same} x the update {create, fast-forward, forced, delete} of refs/heads/patch/a x the caller level {admin, owner, member}: a = controller.Decide(...); assert a is refuse; assert a.message == 'branch is synced from origin; push to ' + shown + ' instead'; assert a.error_type == 'patch_branch'; assert a.message does not contain 's3cret' nor 'bot'

criteria.action: for any decision, read patch_branch_source and push_patches_to_origin from the workspace's settings at the time of that decision, taking hub for a missing patch_branch_source and false for a missing push_patches_to_origin
criteria.contract: two decisions about the same update, with the setting changed between them and no restart, differ as the table of settings says; a workspace whose settings hold neither key is decided as hub/false

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go with an in-memory settings reader: settings = {}; assert Decide(update of patch/a) is allow without forward; settings.patch_branch_source = 'origin'; assert Decide(same update) is refuse with error_type 'patch_branch' and the 'push to' message; settings.push_patches_to_origin = true; assert Decide(same update) is allow with a forward; settings.patch_branch_source = 'hub'; assert Decide(same update) is allow without forward; assert the settings reader was called once per Decide

criteria.condition: the workspace record, the workspace's settings or the patch list cannot be read while a decision is made
criteria.action: report a failure to the rule engine and never answer allow
criteria.contract: Decide returns an error and no answer; through the engine of package 18 the ref update is refused with message 'internal error; try again' and error_type 'internal', which a git client sees on that ref and a source control API caller as HTTP 500 with error_type internal

setup: the real rule engine of internal/gitserver/pushrule with the controller registered
a carry_patch workspace and an update of refs/heads/feature/x that every other rule allows
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table of injected faults {settings reader returns an error; patch store returns an error; workspace record lookup returns an error}: _, err = controller.Decide(...); assert err != nil; then v = engine.Evaluate(request with that update); assert v.Decisions[0].allowed == false; assert message == 'internal error; try again'; assert error_type == 'internal'. One more row: the patch store fails and the ref is refs/heads/deploy -> refused with error_type 'integration_branch' (decided before the patch list is read)

criteria.condition: a caller without the owner exemption pushes an update of a patch branch that the setting protected_branches matches
criteria.action: refuse the update by the protected-branch rule before the controller is asked
criteria.contract: git output holds '<branch> is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)' for a fast-forward and '<branch> is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted' for a forced update or a delete; the controller was asked 0 times; the branch is unchanged

setup: the hub of the integration-branch test; workspace 'demo' with patch 'patch/a', protected_branches ['main', 'patch/*'], patch_branch_source hub
an org member with write access and a PAT carrying git:write
the registered controller wrapped by a counter
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go: table {member fast-forwards patch/a -> 'patch/a is protected; push another branch and open a change (git push -o parley.change)'; member force-pushes patch/a -> 'patch/a is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted'; owner with an API key deletes patch/a -> the same forced-or-delete message}: assert git exit != 0 and out contains the message; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a is unchanged; assert controller call count == 0 after all rows

criteria.condition: the workspace's owner fast-forwards a protected patch branch with an API key while protect.owner_push is true
criteria.action: apply the patch settings to the update after it has passed the protected-branch rule
criteria.contract: patch_branch_source hub: the push is accepted and its parley.git.push event has direct true; patch_branch_source origin with push_patches_to_origin false: git output holds 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead' and the branch is unchanged

setup: the hub and workspace of the protected-branch test above
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go: owner commits on patch/a and runs git push origin patch/a with the API key; assert exit 0; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == local HEAD; assert the last parley.git.push event has metadata.direct == true. Then set patch_branch_source to 'origin' in the workspace's settings; owner commits again and pushes; assert exit != 0; assert out contains 'branch is synced from origin; push to ' + origin URL + ' instead'; assert the hub's branch still equals the first pushed commit

requirements.title: Forwarding a patch branch to origin
requirements.rationale: When origin is the authority and the team still wants to push through the hub, the hub may accept only what origin has accepted first.

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about a create or a non-delete update of the branch of a non-deleted patch while patch_branch_source is origin and push_patches_to_origin is true
criteria.action: answer allow after a forward, and contact origin zero times while deciding
criteria.contract: answer allow with a forward function for that branch and the update's after commit; the origin's request counter is unchanged after Decide

setup: the test origin of internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest with its request counter
settings origin/true, patch 'patch/a' active
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go, a table over the update {create, fast-forward, forced} of refs/heads/patch/a: n = origin.Requests(); a = controller.Decide(...); assert a is allow; assert a.forward != nil; assert origin.Requests() == n

criteria.condition: the controller is asked about a delete of the branch of a non-deleted patch while patch_branch_source is origin and push_patches_to_origin is true
criteria.action: refuse the delete and contact origin zero times
criteria.contract: answer refuse {message: 'branch is synced from origin; delete it on origin instead', error_type: 'patch_branch'}; no forward is attached

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/pushcontrol_test.go beside the forward table: a = controller.Decide(delete of refs/heads/patch/a) with settings origin/true; assert a is refuse; assert a.message == 'branch is synced from origin; delete it on origin instead'; assert a.error_type == 'patch_branch'; assert a.forward == nil; assert origin.Requests() is unchanged

criteria.condition: a forward is run and origin accepts the push
criteria.action: push the update's after commit to refs/heads/<branch> on origin as a non-forced push with the workspace's origin credential resolved at that moment, report success and record that commit as the origin head of the branch
criteria.contract: the forward returns success; origin's refs/heads/<branch> equals the after commit; the recorded origin head of the branch equals the after commit; no other ref of origin changed; the hub's own ref is not written by the forward

setup: the push-accepting test origin with Basic authentication, holding main and patch/a
a hub repository with a commit C on top of origin's patch/a that is not yet the hub's refs/heads/patch/a (an object only)
the workspace's origin credential stored as secret GIT_PAT
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/forward_test.go: refsBefore = origin for-each-ref; hubBefore = hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a; msg, ok = forward(ctx, 'demo', 'patch/a', C); assert ok; assert origin rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == C; assert originHeads.Get('demo', 'patch/a') == C; assert every other ref of origin equals refsBefore; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == hubBefore. Second case: rotate the secret GIT_PAT and the origin's accepted password between two forwards without rebuilding the component -> the second forward succeeds. Third case: the branch does not exist on origin -> the forward creates it

criteria.condition: a forward is run and origin refuses the push or cannot be reached
criteria.action: fail the forward with a scrubbed message that names the reason, and leave the recorded origin head as it was
criteria.contract: the forward returns failure with 'origin rejected push: <reason>'; <reason> is origin's own message for the ref when a rule or hook of origin refused it, 'non-fast-forward' when origin's branch is not an ancestor of the commit, 'authentication failed', 'permission denied', 'repository not found', 'origin unreachable', or 'push failed' for any other failure; the message holds neither the credential's value nor URL user information and is at most 1024 bytes; origin's branch and the recorded origin head are unchanged

setup: the push-accepting test origin with its switches: refuse every update from a hook with a given text, answer a fixed HTTP status, stop listening
origin credential 'tok-12345'
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/forward_test.go, a table of (origin condition -> want message): (hook refuses with 'branch is frozen' -> 'origin rejected push: branch is frozen'); (hook refuses with a text that contains 'tok-12345' -> the message contains '[redacted]' and not 'tok-12345'); (hook refuses with a 3000-character text -> len(message) <= 1024); (origin's patch/a has a commit the pushed commit does not contain -> 'origin rejected push: non-fast-forward'); (HTTP 401 -> 'origin rejected push: authentication failed'); (HTTP 403 -> 'origin rejected push: permission denied'); (HTTP 404 -> 'origin rejected push: repository not found'); (listener closed -> 'origin rejected push: origin unreachable'); (HTTP 500 -> 'origin rejected push: push failed'); in every row: assert ok == false; assert origin's patch/a is unchanged where origin is reachable; assert originHeads.Get('demo', 'patch/a') is unchanged; assert the message contains no '@'

criteria.condition: a forward is run and the workspace's origin credential cannot be read
criteria.action: fail the forward without contacting origin and without an anonymous attempt
criteria.contract: the forward returns failure with 'failed to resolve origin credentials'; the origin's request counter is unchanged

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/forward_test.go: with a credential resolver stub that returns an error: n = origin.Requests(); msg, ok = forward(ctx, 'demo', 'patch/a', C); assert ok == false; assert msg == 'failed to resolve origin credentials'; assert origin.Requests() == n

criteria.condition: a forward has not finished when its limit of 120 seconds passes or when its caller cancels it
criteria.action: end the git push process and fail the forward
criteria.contract: the forward returns failure with 'origin rejected push: timed out'; no git process started by the forward is still running; the recorded origin head is unchanged

setup: the test origin switched to stall every push
the forward component built with a limit of 200 ms in place of 120 s
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/forward_test.go, two rows {the limit passes; the caller's context is cancelled after 100 ms with the limit at 120 s}: start = now; msg, ok = forward(ctx, 'demo', 'patch/a', C); assert ok == false; assert msg == 'origin rejected push: timed out'; assert now - start < 5 s; assert the child git process has exited; assert originHeads.Get('demo', 'patch/a') is unchanged. And assert the hub's component is built with a limit of 120 s by reading the limit from the component the hub composition returns

criteria.condition: a git client pushes two patch branches of a workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin true, and origin accepts the first and refuses the second
criteria.action: refuse the whole push, move no ref of the hub and leave the first branch on origin as forwarded
criteria.contract: git exits non-zero; its output holds 'origin rejected push: <reason>' for the second branch and 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused' for the first; both branches are unchanged in the hub's repository; origin's first branch equals the pushed commit; no parley.git.push event is written

setup: the in-process hub with the controller registered and the push-accepting test origin, whose hook refuses updates of refs/heads/patch/b with 'frozen'
workspace 'demo' with patches patch/a and patch/b, settings origin/true
a local clone with one new commit on each of the two branches
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go: a0, b0 = hub heads of patch/a and patch/b; out, code = git push origin patch/a patch/b; assert code != 0; assert out contains 'origin rejected push: frozen'; assert out contains 'not updated: another ref in this push was refused'; assert hub heads == (a0, b0); assert origin rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == local patch/a; assert count(parley.git.push events) is unchanged

requirements.title: Landing on a patch branch
requirements.rationale: A team that reviews patch work lands it as changes; a landing must not be a way around the rule that decides where patch branches live.

criteria.condition: the guard is asked before the target of a land attempt moves, and the target is not the branch of a non-deleted patch, or the target workspace is not in mode carry_patch, or patch_branch_source is hub
criteria.action: let the attempt pass without contacting origin
criteria.contract: the guard answers allow; the origin's request counter is unchanged

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/landguard_test.go, a table {standard workspace, target main; carry_patch workspace, target main; carry_patch, target the branch of a deleted patch, settings origin/false; carry_patch, target patch/a, settings hub/false; carry_patch, target patch/a, settings hub/true}: n = origin.Requests(); g = guard.BeforeTargetMoves(slug, branch, newHead); assert g is allow; assert origin.Requests() == n

criteria.condition: the guard is asked about a target that is the branch of a non-deleted patch while patch_branch_source is origin and push_patches_to_origin is false
criteria.action: end the attempt as blocked with the reason of the push refusal, so that the target does not move
criteria.contract: the guard answers refuse with the reason 'branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead', <git_url> without user information; origin is not contacted; through package 25 the land attempt's status is 'blocked' and the patch branch keeps its head

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/landguard_test.go: with git_url 'https://bot:s3cret@example.test/acme/demo.git' and settings origin/false: g = guard.BeforeTargetMoves('demo', 'patch/a', newHead); assert g is refuse; assert g.reason == 'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.test/acme/demo.git instead'; assert origin.Requests() is unchanged

criteria.condition: the guard is asked about a target that is the branch of a non-deleted patch while patch_branch_source is origin and push_patches_to_origin is true
criteria.action: forward the new head to origin as a non-forced push under the 120 second limit before the target moves, and let the attempt pass when origin accepts
criteria.contract: the guard answers allow only after origin's refs/heads/<branch> equals the new head; the recorded origin head of the branch equals the new head; the guard itself does not write the hub's ref

setup: the push-accepting test origin holding patch/a
a hub repository with a commit N on top of patch/a, as a land would have built it
settings origin/true
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/landguard_test.go: hubBefore = hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a; g = guard.BeforeTargetMoves('demo', 'patch/a', N); assert g is allow; assert origin rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == N; assert originHeads.Get('demo', 'patch/a') == N; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == hubBefore

criteria.condition: the forward of a land attempt's new head fails because origin refuses it, origin cannot be reached, the origin credential cannot be read or the 120 second limit passes
criteria.action: end the attempt as failed with the error origin_rejected, so that the target does not move
criteria.contract: the guard answers origin rejected, with the forward's scrubbed message; through package 25 the land attempt's status is 'failed' with error 'origin_rejected' and the patch branch keeps its head

setup: the test origin and repository of the passing guard test
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/landguard_test.go, a table over the origin condition {hook refuses with 'frozen'; origin's patch/a moved to a commit N does not contain; listener closed; credential resolver returns an error; origin stalls with the limit set to 200 ms}: g = guard.BeforeTargetMoves('demo', 'patch/a', N); assert g is origin rejected; assert g.message is the forward's message for that row ('origin rejected push: frozen', '... non-fast-forward', '... origin unreachable', 'failed to resolve origin credentials', '... timed out')

criteria.condition: the guard cannot decide because the workspace record, the settings or the patch list cannot be read
criteria.action: return an error to the land engine of package 25 and never an allow, so that the target does not move
criteria.contract: the guard returns an error and none of the answers allow, refuse or origin rejected; origin is not contacted

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/landguard_test.go, a table of injected faults {settings reader fails; patch store fails; workspace record lookup fails}: g = guard.BeforeTargetMoves('demo', 'patch/a', N); assert the guard returned an error and no answer; assert origin.Requests() is unchanged

criteria.condition: a land attempt has moved a target that is the branch of a non-deleted patch
criteria.action: run the rebuild trigger and then the mirror for that branch from the after-landing hook, with the source land and the session id of the landing
criteria.contract: with auto_rebuild_after_push true the rebuild queue receives one request {workspace, submitted_by: 'system:land', session_id: the landing's}; with patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin true origin's branch equals the landed head; the land attempt is answered as landed before the hook has finished

criteria.action: register the guard as a target guard and the trigger as an after-landing hook of internal/land when the hub is composed
criteria.contract: in a composed hub a land onto a patch branch of a workspace with patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false ends with HTTP 409 and a land attempt whose status is 'blocked', and the patch branch keeps its head

setup: the in-process hub with every component of the composition, the test origin as origin and upstream
workspace 'demo' with patch patch/a and settings origin/false; an open change from branch fix/tls targeting patch/a, opened through POST /workspaces/demo/changes
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/push_integration_test.go: before = hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a; r = POST /workspaces/demo/changes/1/land; assert r.status == 409; assert the attempt in the answer has status 'blocked'; assert the answer's text contains 'branch is synced from origin; push to '; assert hub rev-parse refs/heads/patch/a == before; assert the rebuild list of 'demo' is empty

requirements.title: Rebuild trigger after an update of a patch branch
requirements.rationale: The integration branch is stale the moment a patch branch moves; queuing the rebuild is the hub's job, not the pusher's.

criteria.condition: an accepted request updated at least one ref that is not a delete and is the branch of a non-deleted patch, and auto_rebuild_after_push is true or missing from the settings
criteria.action: queue one rebuild for the request through the rebuild enqueue, with the source and the session id of the request
criteria.contract: the enqueue is called exactly once per request, however many patch branches the request updated, with {workspace slug, submitted_by: 'system:push' for a git push and for a source control API write, 'system:land' for a landing, session_id: the request's or null}

setup: a recording rebuild queuer
workspace 'demo' in mode carry_patch with patches patch/a and patch/b active, patch/old deleted
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/trigger_test.go, a table of (updates, source, session, auto_rebuild_after_push -> want enqueue calls): ([update patch/a], push, null, true -> 1 call {demo, 'system:push', null}); ([update patch/a, update patch/b, create feature/x], push, 'sess-1', true -> 1 call with session 'sess-1'); ([create patch/b], push, null, key missing -> 1 call); ([update patch/a], land, 'sess-2', true -> 1 call {demo, 'system:land', 'sess-2'}); trigger.AfterUpdates('demo', updates, source, session); assert the recorded calls equal the wanted ones

criteria.condition: auto_rebuild_after_push is false, or the accepted updates hold no non-delete update of the branch of a non-deleted patch, or the workspace is not in mode carry_patch
criteria.action: queue no rebuild
criteria.contract: the enqueue is called 0 times for: auto_rebuild_after_push false; a delete of a patch branch; an update of the branch of a deleted patch; an update of an unregistered branch or a tag; any update on a standard workspace or a task fork

setup: the recording queuer and patches of the trigger table above
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/trigger_test.go, a table: (auto_rebuild_after_push false, [update patch/a]); (true, [delete patch/a]); (true, [update patch/old]); (true, [create feature/x, create refs/tags/v1]); (true, [update patch/a] on a workspace in mode standard); (true, [update patch/a] on a task fork of 'demo'); (true, []): trigger.AfterUpdates(...); assert queuer.calls == 0 in every row; and on the standard-workspace rows assert the patch store was not read

criteria.condition: the rebuild enqueue reports that a rebuild of the workspace is already queued, running or waiting to retry
criteria.action: skip the trigger silently and go on to the mirror
criteria.contract: no second job is created, no event is written by the trigger, nothing is logged above debug level, and the mirror of the same request still runs

setup: a queuer stub that answers duplicate
settings hub/true and a recording mirror pusher
check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/trigger_test.go: trigger.AfterUpdates('demo', [update patch/a], push, null); assert queuer.calls == 1; assert the event writer stub was called 0 times; assert the captured log holds no record at level warn or error; assert the mirror pusher was called once for patch/a

criteria.condition: the trigger fails because the settings or the patch list cannot be read, the enqueue returns an error, or a step panics
criteria.action: log the failure and return, leaving the refs and the client's answer as they are
criteria.contract: AfterUpdates returns without a panic; one log record at level error names the workspace; the refs the request wrote keep their after values; when only the enqueue failed, the mirror still runs

check.pseudocode: in internal/carrypatch/trigger_test.go, a table of faults {settings reader fails; patch store fails; queuer returns an error; queuer panics}: assert AfterUpdates does not panic; assert the captured log holds one error record containing 'demo'; for the two queuer rows with settings hub/true assert the mirror pusher was called once; for the reader rows assert the queuer and the mirror pusher were called 0 times

criteria.condition: a git push that updated a patch branch has been accepted
criteria.action: run the trigger only after the git client has its complete answer
criteria.contract: the push's HTTP response is complete and git has exited 0 while the trigger is still blocked in the enqueue; after the enqueue is released one rebuild request with submitted_by 'system:push' exists

setup: the in-process hub with the trigger registered as a post-push listener and a rebuild queuer that blocks on a channel
